text:
gpu-monitor-bot: ALERT: Correctable ECC errors above threshold on usw2-pool9-card7 (host=gpu-09-usw2). page_retire_count=23 in last 6h, Xid spikes observed. tagging @infra-oncall

rachel: saw the alert. page_retire_count rising consistent with row remap behavior.

alex: which workloads are pinned on gpu-09? any dedicated/enterprise customers?

devin: short check — from kube node annotations: pods: model-serving-rlhf (3x), embedder-batch (2x), infra-sidecar. No enterprise pin on that node.

samir: recommend immediate cordon + drain. page retire trending upward, could progress to unrecoverable. prefer replacing card rather than waiting for full page retirement.

infra-oncall: agree with drain. propose schedule: cordon now, evict low-priority (embedder-batch) first, then model-serving after warm replicas spin up in pool8. target completion by 11:30 UTC.

alex: can we confirm whether this is a correctable ECC surge (logical) vs actual hardware fault? need to gather dmesg + nvml stats before we RMA.

rachel: collecting logs — posting the most recent kernel lines:
```
[ 4123.812345] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 79, pid=2143, GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 4123.812367] NVRM: RmPciInitPCIForDRV failed for GPU at PCI:0000:3b:00
[ 4130.923456] NVRM: GPU memory ECC corrected error detected at address 0x7ffd1a2c, syndrome 0x2
[ 4201.001234] nvidia: GPU 3: page_retire_cnt=23, remapped_pages=18
```

devin: NVML summary from last 24h:
```
GPU 3: CORR ECC count: 127 -> +60 in 6h
Xid errors: 3 in last hour (transient)
Temperature: 68C
PCI resets: 2
```

samir: that CORR ECC delta is worrying. pattern looks like an expanding bad memory row. RMA likely. Open a hardware ticket and schedule replacement.

infra-oncall: I'll open ticket with vendor (support case #INC-2026-3321) and request expedited RMA. Meanwhile we'll drain and mark node for out-of-service.

alex: ops checklist for drain:
- cordon node: `kubectl cordon gpu-09-usw2`
- evict pods with disruption budgets awareness: `kubectl drain gpu-09-usw2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --pod-selector='priority=low'`
- reroute dedicated customer traffic: update service routing if needed
- collect nvml dump: `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,INFO > /tmp/gpu3-ecc-$(date +%s).log`

rachel: starting drain now. migrating embedder-batch. ping when model-serving replicas are up in pool8.

gpu-monitor-bot: NOTICE: Node gpu-09-usw2 marked CORDONED by infra-oncall at 1782003505. Pods being evicted.

devin: model-serving warm replicas on pool8 are at 2/3. expected to reach 3/3 in ~4m.

samir: once drained, set node label `gpu.health=degraded` and add to replacement queue. I'll attach the nvml logs to the RMA ticket.

infra-oncall: done with drain now (11:28 UTC). node fully drained, cordoned. label applied. vendor ticket opened: INC-2026-3321. ETA replacement 48-72h.

alex: for capacity planning — pool9 has 8 GPUs; with gpu-09 down we lose ~12.5% of capacity in usw2. check scheduled batch jobs and hold noncritical batches until pool9 heals or autoscale picks up.

rachel: adding a short alert rule tweak: lower the CORR ECC delta threshold for pool9 by 30% to catch faster on similar nodes. will open a PR for monitoring rules.

devin: also recommend we add a nightly job to snapshot nvml histograms to detect slow-growing ECC trends. can surface via console.

samir: agreed. long-term we should correlate page_retire_count growth rate with remapped_pages and schedule proactive replacements when slope > 2 remaps/hour.

infra-oncall: noting action items:
- vendor RMA opened (INC-2026-3321) [samir]
- node drained and labeled [infra-oncall]
- monitoring rule PR [rachel]
- nightly nvml snapshot job [devin]
- capacity check + hold noncritical batches [alex]

alex: thanks all. keep thread updated if any regression or new Xid spikes after cordon. :thumbsup:

gpu-monitor-bot: INFO: Thread closed for automated follow-ups. Will re-alert if CORR ECC delta > 30 in 3h.
